title: Localized enriched evaluation of objectwise Kan diagrams
statement:
Use simplicial sets, coherent diagrams and transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the coherent realization adjunction $\mathfrak C\dashv N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and the projective simplicial model and infinity-localization conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] and [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Fix a universe $\mathcal V$; all indexing simplicial sets and values below are $\mathcal V$-small, and all their diagram categories are formed in a containing universe. Let $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ be the simplicial category of Kan complexes with their usual mapping complexes and put $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V})$. For every simplicial set $K$, with no quasicategory assumption, let $\mathsf D_K=\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathfrak C[K],\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})$ have its projective model structure, let $\mathsf D_K^f$ be its ordinary category of objectwise Kan diagrams and enriched natural maps, and let $W_K$ consist of its objectwise weak homotopy equivalences. Denote its infinity localization by $\mathcal L_K=N(\mathsf D_K^f)[W_K^{-1}]_\infty$ and its localization map by $q_K$.

For $P\in\mathsf D_K^f$ define $e_K(P)=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(P)\eta_K:K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, where $\eta_K:K\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathfrak C[K]$ is the adjunction unit. Enriched evaluation also defines its action on ordinary natural maps and their composable chains: an $n$-simplex $P_0\to\cdots\to P_n$ of $N(\mathsf D_K^f)$ is the same as a simplicial functor $\widetilde P:\mathfrak C[K]\times[n]\to\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$, where $[n]$ is the ordered set regarded as a simplicial category with discrete mapping sets, and it is sent to the composite $K\times\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\eta_K\times1}N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathfrak C[K]\times\Delta^n\cong N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathfrak C[K]\times[n])\xrightarrow{N_{\mathrm{hc}}\widetilde P}\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, using that $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ is a right adjoint and is the ordinary nerve on $[n]$. Simplex operators act through $[m]\to[n]$. This gives $e_K:N(\mathsf D_K^f)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. This functor inverts $W_K$. It factors through an equivalence $E_K:\mathcal L_K\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ whose restriction to projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagrams is the enriched-evaluation comparison of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification].

For every objectwise weak equivalence $a:Q\to P$ in $\mathsf D_K^f$, the induced transformation $e_K(a):e_K(Q)\to e_K(P)$ is an equivalence in the entire quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. In particular this holds when $Q$ is projectively cofibrant-fibrant and $a$ is a projective cofibrant replacement map.

source.place: HTT Proposition 4.2.4.4, together with the simplicial-model infinity-localization comparison and its restriction to fibrant objects; evaluation on all objectwise Kan diagrams is an agent-formulated consequence. No Stacks tag. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: Work relative to $\mathcal V$, enlarging only the universe containing the categories. The Kan model category of simplicial sets is combinatorial and simplicial for its usual Cartesian enrichment. Every simplicial set is cofibrant, since its map from the empty set is a monomorphism, and the fibrant objects are exactly the Kan complexes. Thus its bifibrant simplicial subcategory is precisely $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$, and the simplicial-model localization theorem identifies its coherent nerve with spaces. The projective structure on $\mathsf D_K$ supplied by the presentation node is simplicial, with weak equivalences and fibrations objectwise. Its fibrant objects are precisely the diagrams with Kan values, so its ordinary fibrant subcategory is exactly $\mathsf D_K^f$. The coherent nerve of the locally Kan category $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ is a quasicategory; consequently $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ is a quasicategory for every simplicial set $K$.

source.place: Example A.3.2.18; Proposition A.3.3.2; Proposition 1.1.5.10; Scholze, Lecture II, basic fact (1), printed p.14.

proof.text: For a chain $P_0\to\cdots\to P_n$, define $\widetilde P(x,i)=P_i(x)$. On a mapping simplicial set with $i\leq j$, send $f:x\to y$ to $P_j(f)\circ a_{ij}(x)$, where $a_{ij}$ is the composite transformation from $P_i$ to $P_j$; for $i>j$ there is no input. Enriched naturality gives $P_j(f)a_{ij}(x)=a_{ij}(y)P_i(f)$ and therefore makes this assignment preserve compositions and identities. Conversely its restrictions recover the diagrams and the chain. The right adjoint $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ preserves products and equals the ordinary nerve on the discrete enriched category $[n]$. Hence applying it to $\widetilde P$ and precomposing with $\eta_K\times1$ gives exactly the displayed $K\times\Delta^n$ map in the statement. Pulling a chain back along $[m]\to[n]$ gives the same formula with that index map precomposed. This checks all faces and degeneracies, and constructs $e_K$ with its stated object and arrow formulas.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, coherent-nerve adjunction; elementary enriched evaluation on chains.

proof.text: Let $a:Q\to P$ be in $W_K$. Restriction of the map constructed in step 2 to $\{k\}\times\Delta^1$ is the image of $a(k):Q(k)\to P(k)$ in the coherent nerve of Kan complexes. The simplicial-model localization comparison for simplicial sets identifies this canonical map on bifibrant objects with localization, so each weak homotopy equivalence $a(k)$ becomes an equivalence edge of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$. The pointwise-equivalence theorem applies to the entire transformation $e_K(a)$ and to an arbitrary simplicial set $K$: all these components being equivalences implies that $e_K(a)$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. In particular $e_K$ inverts $W_K$, rather than merely giving equivalences between individual evaluated objects.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20; Kerodon Theorem 4.4.4.4 (01DK), pointwise detection of equivalence edges.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathsf D_K^{cf}$, regarded as a full simplicial subcategory, and write $A_0$ for its ordinary category. Apply enriched-diagram rectification with $\mathcal M=\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$, $\mathcal C=\mathfrak C[K]$, and $u=1$. This is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, and the theorem requires no local Kan hypothesis on $\mathfrak C[K]$ and no quasicategory hypothesis on $K$. Step 1 supplies its model hypotheses; the full-chunk convention in that theorem handles the size of the value category. It gives the enriched-evaluation equivalence $\Phi:N_{\mathrm{hc}}A\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. Let $c:N(A_0)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$ be induced by the simplicial functor from the discrete enrichment of $A_0$ to $A$, including each ordinary map as a constant simplex. Then $\Phi c$ is the restriction of $e_K$. Indeed on a chain its $\Delta^n$ parameter is the functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to[n]\to A$; applying enriched evaluation sends a pair of mapping inputs to $P_j(f)a_{ij}(x)$, exactly the formula of step 2. All simplex operators are the restrictions of these same functors, so this identifies the functors on their whole nerves.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Remark 4.2.4.5; Section 1.1.5. Explicit restriction to the ordinary nerve is an elementary evaluation calculation.

proof.text: By the full functor-category universal property of homotopy coherent localization [def-coef-coherent-localization-interface], step 3 gives $E_K:\mathcal L_K\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ with $E_Kq_K\simeq e_K$. Let $\mathcal L_{cf}=N(A_0)[W_{cf}^{-1}]_\infty$, where $W_{cf}$ is the restriction of the projective weak equivalences. Apply the simplicial-model localization theorem to $\mathsf D_K$. Its assertions for the fibrant and bifibrant inclusions give an equivalence $j:\mathcal L_{cf}\simeq\mathcal L_K$ and the canonical equivalence $\lambda:\mathcal L_{cf}\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$ induced by $c$. Step 4 identifies the restrictions of $E_Kj$ and $\Phi\lambda$ to $N(A_0)$. Full faithfulness in that universal property for $\mathcal L_{cf}$ therefore gives $E_Kj\simeq\Phi\lambda$. Both $j$ and $\Phi\lambda$ are equivalences, hence $E_K$ is an equivalence: a quasi-inverse is $j\lambda^{-1}\Phi^{-1}$, with inverse homotopies obtained from this displayed comparison and the inverse homotopies of $j,\lambda,\Phi$. The same comparison proves precisely the claimed agreement with enriched evaluation on projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagrams.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20 and Remark 1.3.4.16, including restriction to fibrant and bifibrant objects and the full localization universal property.

proof.text: Finally a projective cofibrant replacement $a:Q\to P$ of a fibrant diagram may be chosen as a trivial fibration. Its source is cofibrant and is fibrant: $Q\to P\to *$ is a composite of fibrations (solve any lifting problem successively against its two factors). Thus $Q$ is in $A$ and $a$ is an objectwise weak equivalence between Kan-valued diagrams. Step 3 applies verbatim to give an equivalence $e_K(Q)\to e_K(P)$ in the whole functor quasicategory. This also applies to any map satisfying the more explicit hypotheses in the statement, without requiring that it be the chosen functorial replacement.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.16; functorial model factorizations and elementary successive lifting.
